subject: Dedicated capacity: isolation pathway & commitment checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver@novacore.ai>, Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@novacore.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: isolation pathway & commitment checklist

Hi Oliver / Natalie —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. High-level takeaways from the call: 

- Primary pain: unpredictable tail latency and noisy-neighbor interference when you hit bursty traffic (clinical triage peaks).
- Workload profile: ~60–80 inference QPS average, peak bursts to ~220 QPS for short windows tied to shift changes. Typical request size ~350 tokens.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in payloads; must meet strict isolation and audit requirements.
- Business goal: move from experimental self-hosting to a production-ready committed inference environment with clear SLOs and procurement path by end of Q2.

What we proposed on the call (initial recommendation):
- Dedicated pool: start with 4 H100-equivalent GPUs (private, single-tenant pool) with autoscale buckets to 12 GPUs for sustained growth.
- Isolation: VPC + tenant-level encryption, optional on-prem appliance for air-gapped ingestion if you require it.
- SLO targets to hit your immediate needs: monthly uptime SLA 99.95%, p99 generation latency target < 200ms for 512-token requests, and burst capacity available up to 2x committed throughput.
- Cost posture: pilot pricing suggests an exploratory 3-month pilot on 4 GPUs to validate latency + ops-runbook; we’ll follow with a reserved capacity commit (6–12 months) to reduce unit cost.

Immediate asks / proposed next steps: 
1) Please confirm PHI and audit retention expectations (we heard 1 year default; confirm if you need 7+ years).
2) Ben to follow up with an ops playbook + sizing CSV (attached) and a short technical deep-dive date.
3) We will send an SOW draft + MOP (attached) and an initial DocuSign for procurement conditional on security review.

Attachments: redwood_mop_draft.pdf, dedicated-pool-sizing-estimate.csv (first-pass).

Ben (cc) — can you add a short note on quantization/precision tradeoffs for Novacore’s model family?

Oliver / Natalie — if anything below is off, call it out and I’ll update the checklist. If OK, please reply with: (a) confirmation of retention window, (b) security POC who will own the questionnaire, and (c) preferred week for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0104

From: Oliver Stone <oliver@novacore.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@novacore.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 15:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: isolation pathway & commitment checklist

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Retention: security wanted to confirm we’ll get at least 12 months of audit log retention as standard; anything longer we can negotiate but 12 months is a baseline.
- Encryption: is KMS/HSM-backed key management available for both hosted and private deployments? We need to ensure keys are customer controlled.
- VPC/on-prem: we prefer VPC peering initially; on-prem appliance is a fallback if the SOC review requires physical segregation.
- Procurement timeline: our procurement team can get a PO out in ~3 weeks from final SOW, assuming the legal terms don’t require extensive redlines.

I’ve attached the security questionnaire that our InfoSec team uses to triage new vendors (novacore_security_questionnaire.xlsx). Please fill the relevant tabs and return to natalie.

Also: can you provide a brief estimate (ballpark) for monthly cost on the 4→12 GPU path so we can budget ahead of the procurement ping? Even a range is helpful.

Oliver
CTO, Novacore
oliver@novacore.ai

(attachment: novacore_security_questionnaire.xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver@novacore.ai>, Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@novacore.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2027 10:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: isolation pathway & commitment checklist

Hi Oliver / Natalie — Ben from the infra/solutions team here. Quick answers and clarifications inline: 

- KMS/HSM: yes — customer-managed keys supported. For hosted we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault); for Private we can integrate with on-prem HSMs. Keys can be rotated on cadence you define.
- Audit logs: we can retain structured audit logs for 12 months by default and can extend to 7+ years for an additional retention fee and storage SLA. Logs include token counts, request/response metadata (no full payload unless you opt-in), and admin actions.
- VPC & private: VPC peering is supported; Private deployment (VPC or air-gapped) is available under our Private product.
- Latency: our recommended configuration to meet p99 < 200ms at 512 tokens is 4 H100-equivalents with steady-state batching tuned and prefix KV caching enabled.

Pilot commercial suggestion (flexible): 
- 3-month pilot on 4 GPUs (private pool) — objective: validate p99 latency and operational runbook.
- If pilot meets SLOs, transition to 6–12 month reserved commit with autoscale buckets to 12 GPUs.

Ballpark cost (very rough): 4 GPU private pilot ~ $35k–$48k/month depending on model profile and throughput; committed pricing reduces unit cost ~20–35% over pilot rates. We’ll produce a more detailed pricing table after we lock the throughput targets.

Attached: dedicated-pool-sizing-estimate.csv (first-pass numbers) and redwood_mop_draft.pdf (ops runbook).

Next technical step: propose a 45-minute deep-dive with your infra team — topics: VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log schema, and canary/fallback policy. We have availability next Tue (11th) or Wed (12th) morning PT. Which works best?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
(attachment: dedicated-pool-sizing-estimate.csv)
(attachment: redwood_mop_draft.pdf)

Thanks Marissa / Ben — this is helpful and aligns with our internal readout. Quick notes and next steps from Novacore: 

- Security will review the attached questionnaire and the MOP. I’ve looped Natalie to coordinate this — she’ll be the point for InfoSec.
- Procurement expects to be able to issue a PO in ~3 weeks once SOW + DocuSign are in place. Please share the SOW draft and DocuSign link when available.
- Deep-dive: Tue the 11th morning PT works for our infra leads. Please send a calendar invite for 60 minutes (we may extend to include our product manager).

Action items for Redwood: 
1) Fill and return the security questionnaire (Natalie).
2) Share SOW + DocuSign link for pilot commit and pilot pricing table.
3) Confirm deep-dive invite for Tue 11th 9:00 AM PT.

We’re comfortable moving forward with a pilot if the security and SOW gates are clean. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

Oliver
CTO, Novacore
